title: Selling a word nobody knew
lede: Quibi had to explain a new name, a new format and a new habit at the same time. It chose the two most expensive stages in American television to do it, and promoted the platform more than the shows on it.

blocks.title: The Super Bowl and the Oscars
blocks.body:
The first national advertisement ran during Super Bowl LIV on February 2, 2020, two months before anyone could use the product. Quartz put the price of 30 seconds of that game at $5.6 million and reported that viewers said afterwards that they still did not know what Quibi was.[^24] Whitman had said a week earlier: “We have to build a brand—no one’s heard of Quibi—and we have to build the use case.”[^24]

Vulture reported that Quibi also advertised on the Oscars broadcast, and that its marketing “pushed the platform rather than the shows on it.” The magazine’s sources described market research in which 70% of respondents took Quibi for a food-delivery service; a Quibi executive denied that account, and we treat it as unverified.[^4]

The company planned to spend $470 million on marketing in its first year and cut that back once the country was at home.[^5] In late June it switched to promoting individual shows.[^4]

blocks.equation: $1,750M raised[^3] − $350M reportedly returned[^16] = $1,400M. $1,400M ÷ $5.6M per 30-second spot[^24] = 250 spots.
